hook_text: In the 1980s, apartheid tried to reform itself, and it nearly tore the country apart.
clip_script: 1983. The government opens a new Parliament with three houses: white, coloured, Indian. No house for the African majority. The answer comes fast. Hundreds of groups unite as the UDF. Workers build COSATU. In 1984, the townships rise. Rent boycotts. School boycotts. Stay-aways. The government sends in the army, declares a state of emergency, and locks up tens of thousands of people, many of them children. Secret squads kill activists. Some activists kill too. In 1985, President Botha's big speech promises nothing, and an American bank says no more loans. The rand crashes. Companies pack up and leave. Sports teams stay away. The world sings "Free Nelson Mandela". And in a prison cell, Mandela is quietly talking to the government. Something had to give.
visual_style: A parliament building with three doors; a UDF rally with banners; workers marching with COSATU flags; armoured vehicles in township streets; a falling currency chart; a concert crowd holding Free Mandela signs; a prison door slightly open.
mood: Tense and dramatic, ending in suspense.
pacing: Fast and urgent throughout, slowing at the final line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to understand how resistance, repression and world pressure shaped the 1980s.
